newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - December 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - December 2.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail:
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
PREMIER FLAYS LEFT'S CRITICISM OF GOVERNMENT POLICIES

Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda took the left parties to task for criticising the United Front (UF) government at the Janata Dal conclave at Surajkund, near New Delhi. Asking partymen to be tolerant of the criticism raised by the left parties against the government's policies, Gowda described such criticism as mere public posturing. He cautioned the left and other UF partners against criticising the government, and said such action would lead to the fall of the coalition government.
SUMITOMO TO SET UP TWO WHOLLY OWNED SUBSIDIARIES

Japan-based Sumitomo Corporation (SC), one of world's largest trading conglomerates, decided to set up two wholly owned subsidiaries to undertake export-import business and promote joint ventures in India. Sources said the first subsidiary would oversee Sumitomo's operations in South East Asia and monitor the execution of strategic Indian joint ventures in areas such as automotive components, telecom services, hydrocarbons, power and ports. The second subsidiary would operate as a trading company in the field of inorganic and fine chemicals and form joint ventures in this area.
NOTICE TO POWER FIRMS ON PROGRESS OF PROJECTS

In the first instance of its kind, the Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) gave notice to 19 power companies, which were given foreign investment approval, to explain the current progress of their projects. Sources said in the case of projects which had shown little progress, the FIPB would take corrective action and help in getting requisite clearances. Official sources said this would ensure a higher ratio of actual inflow of foreign investment, which was at present only 23 percent to total approvals.

The average daily turnover in non-specified group, accounting for 85 percent of the listed scrips, plunged to the year's low of 100-150 million rupees from 700-800 million rupees at the beginning of 1996. According to Bombay Stock Exchange officials, the average daily turnover in October was 120 million rupees compared to 920 million rupees in January and 510 million rupees in June.
BHEL-SKODA JOINT VENTURE TO MAKE ELECTRICAL TROLLEY BUSES

Czech engineering major Skoda is set to manufacture electric trolley buses in India through a joint venture with public sector major Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd (BHEL). The talks were at an advanced stage and Skoda was hoping to pick up a majority stake in the venture, said Skoda director Martin Basta. The environment-friendly buses that run on electric lines would be manufactured at BHEL's Jhansi plant in Madhya Pradsh, Basta said. Skoda was working out the modalities for transferring technology and hoped to start production within three to four months, Basta added.
ONE PCT CUT IN CASH RESERVE RATIO IN OFFING

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) may effect a further one percentage point cut in cash reserve ratio (CRR) in January 1997. RBI governor C. Rangarajan has said the central bank would cut CRR by another percentage point in January 1997 unless there was an increase in money supply due to increase in foreign exchange assets. The RBI's busy session credit policy was aimed at enhancing the lendable resources available to the banks and reducing the credit cost, Rangarajan said. The previous one percent cut in CRR had led to an increase in lendable resources to banks to the tune of 40 billion rupees, he added.
